name: Change windshield wipers
blurb: Five minutes, no tools, and it costs a fraction of what a garage charges. The only trick is knowing your car’s fitting type.
gear: Correct blades for your car — check the fitment guide
steps: Look up the exact sizes and fitting type for your model; front blades are often two different lengths.
Lift the arm away from the glass and lay a towel on the screen in case it snaps back.
Release the old blade — usually a small tab on a hook fitting, or a clip on a bayonet or pinch-tab fitting.
Slide the new blade on until it clicks, and tug it gently to confirm it is locked.
Lower the arm carefully onto the glass.
Test with washer fluid, and check for streaks or chatter.
tips: A snapped-back arm can crack a windscreen. The towel is not optional.
Streaking after fitting usually means the glass needs cleaning, not that the blades are bad.
proof: New blades fitted, both sides, sweeping cleanly with no streaks or judder.
